locator.section: Eq. 8.2, arrow 2.7, inductive (secondary: C4H9CO+ -> C4H9+ + CO)

evidence.curator_note: adduct corrected to null (convention G): the species undergoing this reaction is an EVEN-ELECTRON cation (charge +1, radical_electrons 0) - a fragment/secondary-fragmentation precursor - NOT the [M]+. radical molecular ion. precursor_mz corrected to the m/z of the ion that actually undergoes the drawn reaction (convention G: the reacting species sets adduct + precursor_mz); it previously carried the neutral molecule's molecular-ion m/z, which describes the parent EI experiment rather than this step's precursor (sibling record IMS8-EQ8.1c already used the reacting-ion convention). (was 100.0883, now 85.0642 = pentanoyl_acylium_cation.) Secondary fragmentation of the m/z-85 acylium: inductive loss of CO regenerates the n-butyl cation C4H9+ (m/z 57). The page prints heats of formation for this arrow but NO abundance percentage, so no relative intensity is recorded (the m/z-57 peak itself is 10% via arrow 2.1). Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs: Eq. 8.2 is a thermochemical fragmentation map (log k printed above each reaction arrow, heats of formation printed below each species), not a curved-arrow figure. All electron moves here are curator-inferred from the mechanism-type label printed under the reaction arrow; none is drawn on the page. ONE double-barbed arrow: the C4-C5 sigma pair collapses onto C5 as the CO carbon lone pair, leaving C4 as the butyl cation (soft lone-pair note expected on C5).

Cross-linked to IMS_8_2_ind_2_7. MISMATCH: the rule's reactant '...[C+]11(...)[C]14[O+]15' is a malformed acylium -- it carries TWO positive charges (C11+ and O15+) and a divalent carbene carbon C14 single-bonded to both C11 and O15, i.e. it is not the singly-charged C4H9-C#O+ (m/z 85) drawn on the page. The correct acylium is encoded here. Listed in rule_mismatches.
